text_blocks.snippet: Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev created the first widely recognized version of the periodic table in 1869.

list.snippet: The Breakthrough: Mendeleev arranged the elements by increasing atomic weight.
Predicting the Unknown: He left intentional gaps in the table for undiscovered elements and accurately predicted their specific chemical properties.

Other Contributors: Earlier scientists like Antoine Lavoisier, John Newlands, and Julius Lothar Meyer also proposed early classification systems or independent tables, but Mendeleev's model had the most lasting scientific impact.

perspectives.author: historyfeelsthepodcast
perspectives.title: Moseley did not create the periodic table itself, that achievement is primarily associated with Dmitri Mendeleev, but he discovered the organizing principle behind its modern form. Earlier periodic tables generally arranged elements according to atomic weight. This produced several awkward inconsistencies where an element’s chemical behavior suggested it belonged somewhere different. In 1913, Moseley used X-ray spectroscopy to measure the unique frequencies emitted by different elements. His experiments demonstrated that every element possessed a distinct atomic number corresponding to the positive charge inside its nucleus. This provided a measurable physical basis for arranging the elements. When ordered by atomic number instead of atomic weight, the table’s inconsistencies disappeared. perspectives.author: physicsfolder
perspectives.title: Mendeleev created the Periodic Table—but he never won a Nobel Prize. 🧪 He was nominated 9 times between 1905 and 1907. In 1906, the Nobel Chemistry Committee actually recommended him, yet the Swedish Academy awarded the prize to Henri Moissan instead. The popular story says scientist Svante Arrhenius personally blocked Mendeleev because Mendeleev had criticized his work. But there’s a catch: Arrhenius wasn’t actually on the Nobel Chemistry Committee. So the viral claim has a true core—but a misleading detail. History is rarely as simple as the viral version. 👀 #DmitriMendeleev #PeriodicTable #Chemistry #NobelPrize

perspectives.author: startupbroclassic
perspectives.title: Dmitri Mendeleev, the man who created the periodic table, was nominated for the Chemistry Nobel nine times between 1905 and 1907, yet never won. In 1906, the committee actually recommended him, only for the prize to go to Henri Moissan instead. The juicy part? Svante Arrhenius, a powerful Swedish chemist whom Mendeleev had criticized, reportedly opposed giving him the prize. The meme exaggerates things by claiming Arrhenius personally blocked him every time, but there really was a scientific feud behind Mendeleev’s bizarre Nobel snub.
